# Necessary response is the weakest sound reading of requirement

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`requirement-is-the-weakest-sound-reading` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](requirement-is-the-weakest-sound-reading.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Over every relation of exchange, necessary response is the weakest reading of requirement that does not read the current level of what is required and under which activity needs support on every run; possible response is not sound.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Necessary response is sound and local, and every sound, local reading of requirement implies it. (`Becoming.ExchangeRelation.Local`, `Becoming.ExchangeRelation.Supports`, `Becoming.ExchangeRelation.respondsBelow_local`, `Becoming.ExchangeRelation.respondsBelow_supports`, `Becoming.ExchangeRelation.respondsBelow_weakest`)
2. Possible response is not sound: under the free relation a formation taking from a condition at nothing possibly responds to it falling below one. (`Becoming.ExchangeRelation.mayRespond_not_supports`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom and no premise.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That requirement is local: that what a formation requires does not read the current level of what is required is argued in the foundation chapter, not proved.
- **Counterexample:** mayRespond_not_supports: possible response under the free relation. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/OverExchange.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
